DESCRIPTION:
Rocky Mountain Cycling Club RMCC
Through the winter months we are doing a mix of rides on the north and south side of the metro area on weekends that are nice enough for a good club ride!

These scenic routes on the southeast side will all have a lot of rolling terrain with some short climbs mixed in. Routes will include Surrey Ridge, the Pinery, Daniels Park, Deerfield and more!

This ride will meet at John Derry Park (just east of I-25/County Line Road) at 9:45 with wheels turning by 10:00.

I will post the route on Wednesday or Thursday once the weather forecast is a little closer in. Generally the routes will be about 50 miles.

Please join us! These off-season rides are always fun and surprisingly challenging!

Non-dues paying members are invited to join us on the rides--once you've done 3 rides with the club we do ask that you join: https://rockymountaincyclingclub.com/

SUMMARY: RMCC Tuesday Night Climbing After Dark!
DESCRIPTION:
Rocky Mountain Cycling Club RMCC
Join us for the RMCC tradition: Tuesday night climbing **after dark!** Sunset may be creeping back to 6 pm, but we don't let that get us down. It's time to grab some lights and keep on climbing. The darkness can't hold us back: we meet at Beverly Heights Park at the base of Lookout every Thursday, weather permitting, until the warmth and daylight returns in the spring. We'll group up about 5:25pm for introductions, route overview, sign-in, and other formalities. We plan to roll at about 5:30.

We'll follow our usual route (see below), though we may make changes depending on weather and road conditions. Snowfall usually melts within a few days, but icy conditions may require riding up or down US 40 instead. Changes will largely be a game-time decision, covered in the route walk-through and potentially adjusted as we progress.

[https://www.strava.com/routes/15959177](https://www.strava.com/routes/15959177)

As is the nature of rides with long climbs, this is a drop then regroup ride. Generally speaking, if you're able to complete Lookout solo in \~30 minutes you'll be able to rejoin at the regroup points. These rides will go at a more conversational pace (for some), and we will roll from the parking area by Buffalo Bill's grave at 6:05. For the sake of the safety and efficiency of the ride, this does mean that we will leave riders behind if they miss the time cut-off. For you Zwifters and powermeter users, a power output of 2.7 w/kg is a good starting point. Expect some separation on the climbs, with opportunities to rejoin at one of several regroup points. Being comfortable in a draft will help on some of the flat / roller sections.
This event will be canceled if weather or roadways are not conducive for a safe, fun ride. We'll cancel as early as possible, however be prepared for game-time calls as conditions can be unpredictable in the foothills.

**Note: Strong, dependable lights are required for this ride.** Also, note that temps at the top in Genesee can be **10-20 degrees cooler** than those at the start, so layering is essential for a successful ride. Gloves (maybe even a light pair and a heavy pair), a hat, shoe covers, and windproof layers have all been used successfully by riders on this ride. Finally, this ride will be canceled if temps at the start are forecast to be below 25 degrees.
We hope to see you out there!

Rocky Mountain Cycling Club RMCC
It's that time of the year again--the RMCC annual jersey order is now ready to go! This year feature the same overall design that we have used the past few years, but with different color options. That should appeal to those looking to buy for the first time and for long-time club members who want a fresh look!
The Alchemist store will be open until November 22nd for us to order clothing for next season.

Here is the link to the store: [https://teamalchemist.com/rmcc/](https://teamalchemist.com/rmcc/)
The password is: RMCC (Note: All caps!)

All clothing items are made-to-order. Delivery is expected in Q1-2027. Alchemist will be handling all of the shipping using USPS Priority Mail.

Items available for sale include:

-4 short-sleeve jersey color options (color block, high-viz yellow, white, and black), available in multiple cuts and sizing.
-Long-Sleeve Thermal jersey in red (unisex sizing)
-Bibs or shorts (men's sizing or women's sizing)
-Warmers (arm, knee, and leg; unisex sizing)
-High vis yellow wind jackets (unisex sizing)
The short-sleeve jerseys are available in both the "Epic Pro" and the "Aero Pro" design. The Aero Pro Race Jersey is based on Pro Tour styling and fit. It features longer, fitted sleeves and a low collar with lay-flat powerband hem. The Epic Pro option is what we have used for many years, with a higher collar and shorter sleeves. The pricing of both options is the same.

The clothing we buy from Alchemist isn't necessarily the cheapest you can buy, but having used them for many years we can attest to the quality and durability of their stuff. I'm still wearing everything I've ever bought from them.

All sales are FINAL! We will NOT accept exchanges or returns. Honestly, when we've tried doing returns in the past it becomes a lot of work to try and resell the items and the club often ends up eating the cost. As we are a break-even operation, we just can't do that going forward. If you do not know your size, please make arrangements with Alchemist to try on samples (https://teamalchemist.com/contact-us/) or contact a fellow club member to try on their clothing.
Questions? Please feel free to message me.
Once again, a big thanks goes out to Jeff at Alchemist and Andrew Dranginis for putting all of this together!

(Note: There is no in-person Meetup for this. This posting is informational only.)
